output.brief: The rejections trace to a setting error on our side, not to the fungicide, Lower Serra fruit or Meridane's equipment. When Meridane bookings moved to the new documentation system, the mandarin product record was copied from the avocado record and kept its 7.0°C carriage temperature. Our specification is 4.0°C. All five Meridane containers sent through the system ran at 7°C and were rejected, with decay of 9–14%. The Meridane container sent before go-live and all three Coastway containers ran at 4°C and passed, whatever the fungicide or transit time. Meridane's units held the temperature we instructed, so a refrigeration claim would fail. Lower Serra pallets were worse inside rejected containers, but they were in every container, so that is secondary. Suspending those growers and withholding payment would punish the wrong party. Confidence is high. What to do now: correct the 7.0°C setting in the mandarin record. Have Meridane reset the container already at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check that compares reefer settings with the product specification before each submission. Hold the claim, the Lower Serra suspension and the invoice deduction. Keep the old fungicide question closed. Loggers are a reasonable extra safeguard.
